answer: Like a nebula condensing, an agent economy can require every new identity to attach a verifiable work receipt before it may trade: the agent must finish a real task - say, labelling a data batch - and have two peers attest the output. Reputation then grows only through sustained honest work, like onyx forming under pressure, and decays without it. One fake identity is cheap, but a thousand means paying for a thousand verified tasks plus attestation fees, while one failed audit burns the basalt-hard history that identity built. Each puppet must earn its standing from scratch, at full price.
